summary: Sidecar header sanitizer strips tenant pin during canary promote, causing mixed model routing
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled canary promote for LumenAI's dedicated pool in us-west, we observed ~12% of tenant requests routed to a different model variant (redwood-v2-medium-quant) despite the tenant being pinned to redwood-v2-medium. Impact: downstream quality alerts and customer request to rollback.

Environment: dedicated cluster tenant=lumenai-prod, edge shard=us-west-2, canary started at 03:14 UTC (5% -> promote to 100%) using canary-coordinator v1.8.2. LumenAI uses a sidecar proxy (lumen-sidecar v0.9.1) that appends tracing metadata and tenant-affinity headers.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger promote from canary to full in console.
2) Customer concurrently ran a batch job increasing per-second requests by ~3x.
3) Edge logs show X-Tenant-Pin header present upstream but missing at router inputs for a subset of requests.
4) Router fallback logic selected older/quantized variant when header absent, causing mixed outputs.

Observed log example: "edge-proxy: header X-Tenant-Pin dropped connID=0432ef metadata_len=278 sanitizer_rule=header_length_regex"
investigation_notes: 2025-01-09 03:22 - Support triaged; initial staging attempts failed to reproduce because sidecar header trimming was not simulated.
2025-01-09 03:40 - SRE (Anika Patel) examined edge-proxy logs and found the header-sanitizer regex matched when header length exceeded 256 bytes (tracing + tenant metadata appended).

2025-01-09 03:55 - Hypothesis: During promote, added tracing IDs from canary-coordinator increased header size; sanitizer dropped X-Tenant-Pin, leading router to treat requests as unpinned and use fallback routing rules.

2025-01-09 04:10 - Router analysis: when X-Tenant-Pin missing, router priority chain may pick a compatible variant (older or quantized) if promoted mapping is not committed atomically across route caches.
2025-01-09 04:45 - Reproduced in canary lab by crafting header payload >260 bytes; confirmed header was stripped and route fell back to prior model id.

2025-01-09 05:30 - Mitigation paths considered: 1) whitelist X-Tenant-Pin in edge-proxy sanitizer, 2) make router consult session-store pin before immediate fallback, 3) pause promote on traffic surge.
2025-01-09 07:00 - Short-term mitigation: disabled regex sanitizer for X-Tenant-Pin on us-west shard and prepared hotfix PR.
comments: 2025-01-09 03:30 - Grace Kim (Support): Customer reported mixed outputs after promote with example request IDs and timestamps; requested rollback if variance persists.
2025-01-09 04:05 - Anika Patel (SRE): Attached correlation IDs and initial analysis showing header drops at edge-proxy; investigating sanitizer rules and sidecar behavior.
2025-01-09 05:15 - Marco Alvarez (Eng): Confirmed reproduction locally by increasing header length via tracing; preparing PR to whitelist pin header and add router guard.
2025-01-09 07:45 - Marco Alvarez (Eng): Deployed edge-proxy hotfix to us-west (PR #4120) that exempts X-Tenant-Pin; monitoring metrics and customer test traffic shows normalization.
2025-01-11 09:10 - Olivia Chen (Customer, LumenAI): Confirmed behavior returned to expected; thanked the team for quick response.
resolution: Root cause: a regex-based header sanitizer in edge-proxy dropped X-Tenant-Pin when sidecar tracing metadata made header length exceed a threshold during a traffic surge at promote. This caused router to consider requests unpinned and fall back to older model variants. Fixes deployed: 1) hotfix to edge-proxy to whitelist X-Tenant-Pin (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4120) rolled to us-west at 07:45 UTC and staged for global rollout; 2) router guard change to consult session-store pin before fallback (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/289). Rollout notes: global edge rollout scheduled 2025-01-12 behind a feature flag with canary. Follow-ups: add automated canary-promote tests for large header payloads, add a runbook step to pause promotes on traffic spikes, and track a backlog task to remove header-length heuristics affecting routing headers (INT-1104).
